# African American Civil Rights Movement

> > A comprehensive educational resource documenting the African American struggle for civil rights, from slavery abolition through the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s-60s.

This site is a UMass History Club student project exploring key figures like Martin Luther King Jr., Frederick Douglass, and Harriet Tubman, landmark Supreme Court cases including Brown v. Board of Education and Plessy v. Ferguson, and pivotal organizations such as the NAACP and SNCC. It covers the fight against Jim Crow laws, segregation, and the journey toward equal rights through nonviolent resistance and legislative action.

## Key Topics

- Martin Luther King Jr.
- Brown v. Board of Education
- Jim Crow laws
- NAACP (National Association for the Advancement of Colored People)
- SNCC (Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee)
- Frederick Douglass
- Harriet Tubman
- Fourteenth Amendment
- Emmett Till
- Nonviolent resistance
- Segregation and racial segregation
- Reconstruction era
- Civil Rights Act of 1964
- Student activism and sit-in movements
- Slavery abolition

## Movement Overview

- [What is the African American Civil Rights Movement?](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/what-is-african-american-civil-rights-movement/): African American Civil Rights Movement overview with Plessy v. Ferguson
- [What is the Civil Rights Movement?](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/what-is-the-civil-rights-movement/): Overview of Civil Rights Movement featuring Douglass, Tubman, and Harrison
- [Timeline](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/timeline/): Chronology from 13th Amendment through Jim Crow and Reconstruction era

## Key Events and Actions

- [I Have a Dream](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/i-have-a-dream/): MLK's 1963 March on Washington speech and the Emancipation Proclamation
- [Sit-In Movement](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/sit-in-movement/): Greensboro sit-ins and nonviolent lunch counter protests of the 1960s

## Legislation and Policy

- [Civil Rights Act of 1866](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/civil-rights-act-of-1866/): Reconstruction-era legislation by Trumbull, vetoed by Andrew Johnson
- [Affirmative Action](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/affirmative-action/): Affirmative action policy under Lyndon Johnson and Civil Rights Act 1964

## About

- [About Us](http://www.african-american-civil-rights.org/contact/): UMass History Club student project on civil rights history
